title: Make the deliverables list the single statement of file scope
summary: Retry of r2d0 without any text-matching of criteria. The reader prompt says scope comes only from the deliverables list; code adds CHANGELOG.md to change readings when missing, with a 'changelog' default; the verifier's brief says a file outside the list is the scope finding, judged against the list.

defaults_applied.how: The deliverables list becomes the single statement of scope, so criteria cannot contradict it, instead of patching each contradiction.
Unit tests cover the CHANGELOG addition and the false-positive cases that sank r2d0.
One focused change across the prompt, the reading builder and the verifier brief.
The CHANGELOG default is enforced in code when the reading is built; the scope sentences are prompt text, marked as prose-only.
Details came from the repository: BRIEF.md line 337, reader.md, reading.rs build_reading, and the prompt token budget in lib.rs.
Comments, changelog and decision entries are written for an outside reader.

assumptions: The repository is at the state before r2d0: no check_scope_consistency exists in reading.rs.
'The verifier's brief' means the brief text built in briefs.rs. If the text actually lives in verifier.md, the sentence goes there.
The added CHANGELOG.md deliverable is for readings whose capability is change, including declined ones only if they have capability change; study and null-capability readings are untouched.
The 'changelog' default is added by code as a defaults_applied entry with its own text citing BRIEF.md. It does not need an entry in defaults.toml, which is governance and stays unchanged.

The reader prompt gains one line and stays under budget without trimming other lines. If it does not fit, the lib.rs budget check will show it and the producer must pay with removals that keep every line's meaning.

acceptance_criteria.text: crates/athena-context/prompts/reader.md adds one line saying file scope is given only by the deliverables list and acceptance criteria never restate which files may change. Every existing line keeps its meaning and wording, and the added text fits the reader prompt budget enforced in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs.

In crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs, build_reading appends CHANGELOG.md (action modify, with a stated probability) to the deliverables of a reading with a capability of change when it is missing, and adds a defaults_applied entry with id 'changelog' whose text cites BRIEF.md's 'tagged releases and a changelog'. It leaves a reading that already lists CHANGELOG.md, and any non-change reading, untouched.
No code inspects the wording of acceptance criteria to judge file scope. There are no keyword or window matches on criterion text, and no new rejection of readings based on their criteria.

The verifier's brief (crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs, or the verifier prompt if that is where the brief text lives) says a changed file outside the deliverables list is the scope finding, judged against the list and not against criterion wording.

New unit tests cover: CHANGELOG.md added when missing; no duplicate when present; no addition for a non-change capability; the 'changelog' default added once; a reading whose criteria mention CHANGELOG.md, 'exclud' or 'not' is accepted unchanged; the verifier brief contains the scope sentence. Run: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt --check. All pass.
CHANGELOG.md gains an entry for this change, and docs/decisions.md records the call, including why the criteria-text heuristic was dropped.

out_of_scope: Any text-matching or heuristic check of acceptance-criteria wording
Rejecting readings at parse or admission time because of scope wording
Rewording or shortening existing reader prompt lines
Changes to athena.toml, CI workflows, or other governance files
departures: Slightly higher than the reference: the change touches prompts, builder code, the verifier brief and tests, and prompt-budget fitting may need an extra pass.
